clue.text: Something Hollywood's good at — with reference to moving TV show

indicators.note: moving says these two letters shift from their place to another spot in the phrase

parts.note: Paul Hollywood, the TV baker, is good at baking bread
RE is the short form meaning with reference to, as in a memo's subject line

explanation.surface: A tribute to Hollywood's talent, apparently citing an emotionally moving television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Hollywood is the baker who judges The Great British Bake Off. Take the RE out of BREAD and put it after the first B of BAKING to turn BAKING BREAD into the show's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking Bad is the American crime drama series about Walter White, a chemistry teacher turned drug manufacturer.

clue.text: See 1
Dropping minute, possibly titanium bone discovered in ancient Rome and elsewhere

indicators.note: dropping says the minute's letter falls out of the word for the metal

parts.note: titanium is one example of a metal

indicators.note: discovered means the bone has its covering stripped off, losing its first and last letters

parts.note: the tibia is the shinbone

explanation.surface: An archaeologist, dropping a minute piece of titanium, finds a bone in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: METAL without M gives ETAL; TIBIA without its outer letters gives IBI. The Latin phrase is guessable from the everyday word alibi.
explanation.definitionFit: Et alibi is Latin for 'and elsewhere', the sort of phrase a Roman would use, now found in scholarly references.

clue.text: Recognised Kim Wexler principally defending any outspoken …

indicators.note: defending means the two initials stand guard around the other piece
principally takes the leading letter of each of the two names
outspoken says we want what the word sounds like when spoken

parts.note: the word any, spoken, sounds like the letters N and E said one after the other

explanation.surface: In Better Call Saul, Kim Wexler, the lawyer, recognised for defending anyone, speaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the letters N-E aloud and you hear 'any'. The ellipsis runs the sentence on into the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To have recognised someone is to have known them, the past tense of know in its identifying sense.

clue.text: … criminal with long sentence, initially they'll stay up late

indicators.note: criminal here says the letters are crooked, out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of sentence

explanation.surface: A convict serving a long sentence, at first, can't sleep and stays up late.
explanation.definitionFit: Night owls are people who habitually keep late hours, staying awake well into the night.

clue.text: Alcohol-free ale's bringing in punter

indicators.note: bringing in says the beer takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
TT is teetotal, so alcohol-free

explanation.surface: A low-alcohol ale is attracting a new kind of customer to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for teetotal. A punter, in British usage, is someone who places a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A better is one who bets, the same as a punter in British gambling slang.

clue.text: Every now and then Pepsi pays for spot

indicators.note: every now and then takes only some letters, alternating along the phrase

explanation.surface: Pepsi occasionally pays for an advertising spot on television.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of 'Pepsi pays'. 'Spot' looks like an advertising slot, but it is the verb meaning to catch sight of.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy something is to catch sight of it, a literary synonym for seeing or noticing.

clue.text: Sinatra excited empress

indicators.note: excited suggests the singer's letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra got an empress all excited.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar or a female ruler of Russia, an empress in rank.

clue.text: Discharge high explosive during game with Mike

indicators.note: during says the explosive is placed within the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game
Mike is the radio alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: Someone sets off high explosive during a game with Mike, Walter White's associate in Breaking Bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose, the kind that collects as sleep.

clue.text: Stoic and composed felon, Gus Fring

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Gus Fring, the drug lord of Breaking Bad, is described as a stoic, composed criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stoic endures hardship patiently without complaint, which is exactly what a long-suffering person does.

clue.text: Copy doctor opening curtain

indicators.note: opening says the doctor's letters come at the start

parts.note: to ape is to copy or mimic

explanation.surface: A doctor copies someone opening a curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a long heavy curtain, the usual American word for one.

clue.text: Teams possibly fighting on party drug

indicators.note: on says the fighting follows the party in an across answer

parts.note: a party is a group of people
fighting is war
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Teams of people are fighting on, after a party where drugs were taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teams' looks like sports sides, but it is Microsoft Teams, the office collaboration program.
explanation.definitionFit: Groupware is software for collaborative work, and Microsoft Teams is a familiar example of it.

clue.text: Perhaps Bob Odenkirk's biggest character's framed by cleaner

indicators.note: framed by says the cleaner's letters surround the other piece

parts.note: Cif is a brand of household cleaning product
the capital letter at the start of Odenkirk is its biggest letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Biggest character' looks like the actor's best-known role, but it is the capital O of his name. 'Bob' is a haircut, not the actor's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A coif is a hairstyle, and a bob is one example of a hairstyle.

clue.text: Two firms meet over a drink

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm, and two of them gives this

explanation.surface: Executives from two companies meet up over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot drink made from powdered cacao beans and milk.

clue.text: Produce a drug with value — finally on street

indicators.note: on says the other letters follow the street in an across answer
finally takes the closing letter of both drug and value

explanation.surface: Instructions to produce a valuable drug and sell it on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' applies to both 'drug' and 'value', though 'with' sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a play or show is to produce it, putting it on before an audience.

clue.text: See 17
Country's ultimately the wrong way up on back of chart

indicators.note: ultimately takes the closing letter of each of the four words that follow
back of takes the closing letter of chart

explanation.surface: A country appears upside down on the back of a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way up' looks like a reversal instruction, but it is just four words whose last letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is the North African nation on the Nile, a country.

clue.text: Wild time in Florida

indicators.note: in says the time sits inside the state's letters

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having a wild time on holiday in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Feral describes an animal living untamed in nature, so wild.

clue.text: Chuck McGill — fine without source of electricity — one can see right through it

definitions.text: one can see right through it

indicators.note: chuck means throw, so these letters are tossed about into a new order
without says a letter is taken away from fine
source of takes the first letter of electricity

explanation.surface: Chuck McGill, of Better Call Saul, believes he is fine without electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like Chuck McGill's first name, but it is the anagram signal. In the show he believes he is allergic to electricity, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Cling film is transparent plastic wrap for food, so it is easy to see through.

clue.text: Desert seen when Walt and Jesse regularly cooked

indicators.note: cooked here means doctored, so the letters are rearranged
regularly takes the alternate letters of Jesse, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Walt and Jesse, of Breaking Bad, cooked their drugs out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Walt and Jesse cook methamphetamine in the New Mexico desert in Breaking Bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasteland is a barren, empty landscape, which is what a desert is.

clue.text: See 9
Live band's extreme sound

indicators.note: extreme takes the far end letter of band

explanation.surface: A live band's sound is extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like an adjective for a concert, but it is the verb meaning reside.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live or reside there.

clue.text: In reference to a rugby player — round and very strong

parts.note: a prop is a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum
O is round in shape
so is a word for very
F is forte, strong or loud in musical notation

explanation.surface: A description of a rugby player who is round and very strong.
explanation.walkthrough: A prop is the position in a rugby scrum usually taken by the heaviest, strongest players.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos of means concerning or with reference to something just mentioned.

clue.text: Informal time for kiss identified

indicators.note: for says the time goes in place of the kiss

parts.note: relaxed means informal or casual
X is a kiss in letters

explanation.surface: An informal time for a kiss has been identified.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate to someone is to identify with them, so related matches identified in that sense.

clue.text: Moderate hit set in outskirts of Albuquerque

outskirts of takes the first and last letters of Albuquerque

parts.note: to bat is to hit

explanation.surface: A moderate hit was filmed on the outskirts of Albuquerque, where Breaking Bad is set.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or moderate something, as a storm or pain does.

clue.text: A shy person, largely accepting men will be passionate

indicators.note: accepting says the shortened word takes the men inside it
largely means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a mouse is a timid, shy person
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A shy person, for the most part, will become passionate once accepting men.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means showing romantic or sexual desire, so ardent or passionate.

clue.text: Dub some anatomical language

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A request to name some of the language of anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dub someone is to give them a name, as to call them something.

clue.text: Mafia boss with term in prison — he's emasculated

indicators.note: term means end, so the closing letter of prison

explanation.walkthrough: 'term in prison' reads as a sentence, but 'term' is the end of the word prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel, fattened for the table.

clue.text: Wakes up lopsided

indicators.note: up here means in disorder, as in things being all up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wakes up and finds themselves lopsided.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew means crooked or not straight, so lopsided.

clue.text: Old king left after cycling America

indicators.note: after says the left comes behind the cycled letters
cycling moves the first letter round to the end

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

explanation.walkthrough: Saul is also Saul Goodman, the lawyer in the Breaking Bad theme, though here the definition points to the biblical king.
explanation.definitionFit: Saul was the first king of Israel in the Old Testament, so an ancient king.

clue.text: Some people dig this El Camino broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'dig' looks like slang for enjoy, which suits a film; it is literal digging.
explanation.definitionFit: Miners dig coal out of a coal mine, which is the pit they work in.

clue.text: So good to get away from ruffians

parts.note: thugs are ruffians

Some butter pastry shortened with occasional doses of plain oil

parts.note: choux is a light pastry used for eclairs

explanation.walkthrough: 'plain oil' looks like one ingredient, but 'oil' is the definition and 'plain' alone gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchouli is an aromatic essential oil from an Asian shrub, used in perfume.

clue.text: I stridently shout becoming closer to Walter White?

clue.text: Melting 6 pence down, ok

clue.text: Fearsome females from Sierra Leone returned after knocking out international opponents

indicators.note: after says the opponents come behind the reversed letters
returned says the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: Sierra is the radio alphabet word for S

indicators.note: knocking out says the international letter is removed from the director's name

parts.note: Sergio Leone was the Italian director of spaghetti westerns
E and S, East and South, are opponents in bridge

explanation.surface: Fearsome women from Sierra Leone return home after defeating international rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sierra Leone' looks like the country, but it splits into S and Leone, the director Sergio. SERGIO without I gives SERGO; S plus SERGO reversed gives OGRESS. In bridge, East and South sit next to each other at the table, so they are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogresses are female ogres, monstrous giantesses of folklore, so frightening women.
